item.title: Getting closer
item.description:
Source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/kellyphillipserb/2025/12/22/a-simple-postmark-change-could-affect-your-taxes-and-charitable-giving/ Archive paywall bypass source: https://archive.ph/t66bh Excerpt: As a first-year law student, I learned it this way: If a piece of mail is properly addressed with the correct amount of postage and dropped in the mailbox, the postmark stamped on the envelope is generally considered the date of filing (or, in contract law, the date that an offer was made). Today, the mailbox rule can also apply to other means of communication, such as fax, telegram, or email. The concept is particularly important in the tax world. It was memorialized in 1954 when Section 7502 became part of the tax code. Now, by law, a tax return or payment is considered filed on the date of the U.S. postmark, not the date of receipt by the IRS. This means taxpayers can mail returns and checks up to—and including—the filing deadline, confident that a timely postmark will protect them from penalties and interest. The mailbox rule has been relied upon in tax audits and in Tax Court for years. The Big Change A recent change in USPS processing rules could change all of this. The USPS has now clarified that most postmarks reflect the date of postal processing, not necessarily the date a mailpiece was deposited by the sender. According to the USPS, because most postmarks are applied at processing facilities, they do not necessarily represent either the place at which, or the date on which, the Postal Service first accepted possession of the mail piece. This means the date stamped by a postmark applied at a processing facility may be later than the date the mailpiece was first accepted by the Postal Service. The change, published in the Federal Register on November 24, 2025, is effective as of December 24, 2025.

item.description:
The boys still do not recognize this as a bed they can get inside. It's just for sitting on. And they are always right.
Little Bear, big bed :D
Beginning of the laze...
Social laziness
Sun baths
Sleepy Salerno
Salerno sandwich lol
Monday morning cuddles(bear censoring a nipple)
Bob alert!
Found a different lantana bush on my skate today, on a road I haven't skated in a while. I think I remember it, I don't think it's a new discovery. But it's got gorgeous flowers
Roses are not my favorite, not even close, and yet we have some lovely rose bushes dotted around town. Fun longboarding sidenote I want to share with y'all: so when I started my skate today I immediately realized something was wrong with my board. Super wobbly. I could not control the board over 20mph. I thought the trucks had loosened up but when I flipped it over I found that one of my pivot cups in one of the trucks had deteriorated and most of it fell out. So I skated to my favorite local boardshop: NC Boardshop. The staff are awesome and have helped me with donations to a non-profit that I worked with in the past. They didn't have the right size, but they gave me one that was pretty close. They even called some of the skate shops in Santa Cruz to see if they carried the right size, but no luck. So we put a smaller pivot cup in. "MacGuyver'd" we said. And it worked fantastically!!! I was afraid I was gonna have to head home early but because of their efforts I hit all my favorite spots and skated for another 4 hours!!! I called them twice that afternoon to say thanks; once when I skated down the hill in front of their shop to let them know it seemed to be working, and at the end of my session to let them know they totally saved my day. TLDR: local skate shop rescued my day, and my health and safety :)

item.description: Construction crews at the White House are working 20 hours a day on a ballroom the Chief Justice says is likely illegal. Five justices let the work continue Monday by ruling that nobody has the right to sue over it, but never decided whether the ballroom is legal. Chief Justice John Roberts wrote that federal law forbids erecting a building on park grounds in Washington without express authority from Congress, and Congress has passed no such law. Donald Trump won again by ignoring the rules and building faster than the courts could stop him.
